title: 3 Things You Must Do On The First Day Of School https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2018/08/18/3-things-you-must-do-on-the-first-day-of-school/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Rejecting the common tendency to rush through every policy on day one, Linsin argues teachers only truly need to nail three things: one great overview of the classroom management plan, one great routine, and one great lesson. For the overview, he recommends a 20-30 minute walkthrough that explains the plan's purpose, reads it aloud, briefly describes each rule and consequence, and 'visualizes' the experience of a misbehaving student stepping through consequences. For the first routine—ideally the opening minutes of class—he emphasizes highly detailed modeling since the first routine sets the standard for how all future routines will be taught, with different modeling intensity recommended by grade band. For the lesson, he urges teachers to choose one clear, challenging objective and teach it with full passion and performance, since students are most open to influence on day one. Together, he argues, these three elements establish classroom culture more powerfully than any amount of rushed policy coverage.
points: Rather than rushing through every policy, Linsin argues teachers should focus on three things on day one: one overview, one routine, one lesson.
The classroom management plan overview (20-30 minutes) should explain its purpose, read the plan aloud, and 'visualize' a misbehaving student's path through consequences.
The first routine taught sets the model and standard for how all subsequent routines will be learned, with modeling intensity varying by grade band.
For the day's lesson, teachers should choose one clear, worthwhile objective and teach it with full passion since students are most receptive on day one.
These three elements are framed as establishing classroom culture more effectively than attempting to cover every policy and procedure on the first day.
quotes: The tendency is to rush. To try and cover every policy and procedure. To cram it all in on the first day of school for fear that if you don’t, then your students will develop bad habits.
But the truth is, you only really need to focus on three things.
It’s best to start by explaining why you have a classroom management plan to begin with and how it protects their right to learn and enjoy school.
That first routine you teach, however, is especially important because it provides a model for how all other routines should be performed.
You see, on the first day of school your students are most open and ready to learn. They’re eager to turn over a new leaf and you must take advantage of it.

So double-down on what matters most. Teach boldly and courageously. Leave your students at the end of the first day excited, happily shaken, and wholly different than when they walked through your door.
